correctness.rationale: Exact finite-section kernel normalization gives angle-independent diagonal entries n(t^k/k!)/F_m(t). Rayleigh and Hadamard bounds are attained by regular polygons; equality requires vanishing power sums, forcing regularity by Newton identities. Strictly monotone envelope ratios give the unique minimax radius T_m, while differentiating the determinant gives the unique truncated-Poisson mean root S_m. Pairing factorial factors proves S_m>T_m for m>=3. Stirling and an exponentially small truncated-Poisson boundary correction yield the stated asymptotic ratio. The embedded numerical checker reconstructs the actual sampling matrix and verifies 341 cases (maximum regular-spectrum error 3.55e-15), solely as corroboration. No unrestricted planar optimum, arbitrary weights, or independent audit is asserted.

value.rationale: Optimizing a finite-dimensional Gaussian Fock evaluation system under a natural exactly one-ring geometric constraint is a precise information/reconstruction design problem. The theorem classifies all angular and radial optimizers simultaneously for worst-case stability versus information-volume criteria, proves their exact strict divergence, and quantifies a dramatic exp((1/2-1/e)m) squared-conditioning penalty from choosing the D-optimal design. This substantive general all-degree tradeoff is not a normalization-only observation, ad hoc numerical slice, or restatement of Fourier diagonalization.
